Step 1: Visit an Enrolment Centre

The first step is to locate an Aadhaar enrolment centre near you. You can find the closest centre by checking the official Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) website (uidai.gov.in) or by calling the Aadhaar helpline.

Step 2: Fill the Application Form

At the enrolment centre, you’ll be required to fill out an application form. Make sure to carry the necessary documents, such as your own Aadhaar card (if you have one) and your baby’s birth certificate or hospital discharge certificate.

Step 3: Remember to Provide a Mobile Number

When filling out the application form, ensure that you provide a valid and active mobile number. This is crucial because all Aadhaar-related updates and notifications will be sent to this registered mobile number.

Step 4: Capturing Your Baby’s Photo and Biometrics

The enrolment operator will click your baby’s photograph and capture their biometric data (fingerprints and iris scan) at the centre. It’s essential to ensure that your child’s face is clearly visible in the photograph, as this will be used for biometric verification in the future. For babies aged 0-5 years, biometric data may not be captured due to their small fingerprints and underdeveloped irises.

Step 5: Biometric Authentication for a Parent/Guardian

One of the parents or guardians must have an existing Aadhaar card for biometric authentication. This step is necessary to establish the relationship between the child and the parent or guardian.

Step 6: Collect Acknowledgement Slip

After completing the enrolment process, you’ll receive an acknowledgement slip. This slip serves as proof of your baby’s Aadhaar enrolment and should be kept safe until you receive the Aadhaar card.

Step 7: Aadhaar Generation Notification

Once your baby’s Aadhaar is generated, you’ll receive a notification on the registered mobile number. This notification will contain the Aadhaar number and other relevant details.

Step 8: Check Data and Confirm

When you receive the notification, make sure to cross-check all the details, such as your baby’s name, date of birth, and address. If everything is correct, you can confirm the data, and the Aadhaar card will be dispatched to the registered address.

Also Read:

Additional Important Points

1. Biometric Updates: As your child grows older, their biometric data (fingerprints and iris scans) will need to be updated periodically.
